steps.note: Roll the app so new guest orders store '' instead of NULL. Nothing in the database has changed yet, so old and new pods both work during the rollout.
Let the last in-flight requests from the old pods finish.

Add CHECK (email IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID. From now on no NULL email can be written, but existing rows are not checked yet. This needs a brief ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, so each attempt waits at most 100 ms (shorter than the app's 2 s timeout) and gives up, then retries, so app queries never pile up behind it.
steps.sql: DO $$ DECLARE i int := 0; BEGIN LOOP BEGIN PERFORM set_config('lock_timeout', '100ms', true); ALTER TABLE orders ADD CONSTRAINT orders_email_not_null CHECK (email IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID; EXIT; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN i := i + 1; IF i >= 100 THEN RAISE; END IF; PERFORM pg_sleep(0.2 + random() * 0.3); END; END LOOP; END $$;

steps.note: Backfill: set email = '' on the guest orders that have NULL, in batches of 50,000 ids, one commit per batch with a short pause. The app only inserts and reads, so these row locks never block it. Only rows that are NULL are touched; no other column or row changes. The upper bound is read after the constraint is in place, so every row above it already has an email.
steps.sql: DO $$ DECLARE lo bigint := 0; hi bigint; BEGIN SELECT coalesce(max(id), 0) INTO hi FROM orders; WHILE lo <= hi LOOP UPDATE orders SET email = '' WHERE id >= lo AND id < lo + 50000 AND email IS NULL; COMMIT; PERFORM pg_sleep(0.05); lo := lo + 50000; END LOOP; END $$;

steps.note: Validate the constraint: one full scan proving there are no NULLs left. It takes only a SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE lock, which does not block the app's reads or inserts. Fails (and stops the plan) if any NULL were left.
steps.sql: ALTER TABLE orders VALIDATE CONSTRAINT orders_email_not_null;

steps.note: SET NOT NULL. Postgres 17 uses the validated CHECK constraint to prove there are no NULLs and skips the table scan, so the ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock is held only for a moment. Then drop the now-redundant CHECK in the same transaction. Same short lock_timeout with retry as above.
steps.sql: DO $$ DECLARE i int := 0; BEGIN LOOP BEGIN PERFORM set_config('lock_timeout', '100ms', true); ALTER TABLE orders ALTER COLUMN email SET NOT NULL; ALTER TABLE orders DROP CONSTRAINT orders_email_not_null; EXIT; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN i := i + 1; IF i >= 100 THEN RAISE; END IF; PERFORM pg_sleep(0.2 + random() * 0.3); END; END LOOP; END $$;

steps.note: Check the result: orders.email is NOT NULL.
steps.sql: DO $$ BEGIN IF NOT (SELECT attnotnull FROM pg_attribute WHERE attrelid = 'orders'::regclass AND attname = 'email') THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'orders.email is not NOT NULL'; END IF; END $$;
